items.answer: Half of the rounding unit (10 cm) is 5 cm, so the bounds are 15 cm ≤ L < 25 cm.
items.markingKey: Half of the rounding unit (10 cm) is 5 cm, so the bounds are 15 cm ≤ L < 25 cm. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Noah writes: "(2x)³ = 2x³." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³.
items.markingKey: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why it is easier to find 8^(2/3) by taking the cube root first.
items.answer: 8^(2/3) = (∛8)² = 2² = 4; rooting first keeps the numbers small, whereas 8² = 64 then ∛64 = 4 needs a bigger root.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: 8^(2/3) = (∛8)² = 2² = 4; rooting first keeps the numbers small, whereas 8² = 64 then ∛64 = 4 needs a bigger root. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Without a calculator, explain which number is larger: 1.2 × 10³ or 5.3 × 10⁰. By roughly what factor is it larger?
items.markingKey: Compare powers of ten first, then the front numbers if needed (R1); 1.2 × 10³ is larger (A1); factor ≈ 2.3e+02 (A1).

items.stem: Two lengths are a = 73 cm and b = 20 cm, each to the nearest cm. Diego says the maximum value of a − b is 73.5 − 20.5. Explain the mistake and give the correct maximum.
items.markingKey: To maximise a difference subtract the smallest b: UB(a) − LB(b) (R1) = 73.5 − 19.5 = 54 cm (A1).

items.stem: Tomás writes: "(2x)³ = 2x³." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³.
items.markingKey: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Evaluate 64^(2/3) without a calculator.
items.markingKey: 3-th root of 64 = 4 (M1); raise to power 2: 16 (M1) = 16 (A1).

items.stem: Calculate (4.3 × 10⁸) × (4.0 × 10¹), giving your answer in standard form to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: Multiply the numbers (17.2) and add the powers (M1); adjust so 1 ≤ a < 10: 1.72 × 10¹⁰ (A1).

items.stem: A rope is 10 m, correct to the nearest 10. Write down the limits of accuracy as an inequality.
items.markingKey: Half the unit is 5; lower bound 5, upper bound 15 (A1 each); correct inequality signs (A1).

items.stem: Priya writes: "(2x)³ = 2x³." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³.
items.markingKey: The power applies to every factor in the bracket: (2x)³ = 8x³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Evaluate 8^(−2/3) without a calculator.
items.markingKey: 3-th root of 8 = 2 (M1); raise to power 2: 4 (M1); negative index → reciprocal 1/4 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims that (3 × 10⁴) × (4 × 10⁵) = 12 × 10⁹, which is in standard form. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.markingKey: 12 × 10⁹ must be adjusted to 1.2 × 10¹⁰. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A plank is 2 cm, correct to the nearest whole number. Write down the limits of accuracy as an inequality.
items.markingKey: Half the unit is 0.5; lower bound 1.5, upper bound 2.5 (A1 each); correct inequality signs (A1).
Write 16 as 2⁴ (M1): 2^(4x) = 2^(2x + 3); equate indices 4x = 2x + 3 (M1); x = 3/2 (A1).

items.stem: Solve x^(2/2) = 25 for x > 0.
items.markingKey: Raise both sides to the power 2/2 (M1): x = 25^(2/2) = (2-th root of 25)² = 5² (M1) = 25 (A1). Check: (2-th root of 25)² = 5² = 25 (R1).

items.stem: A virus particle is 1.2 × 10⁻⁷ m long and a dust mite is 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m long. How many times longer is the dust mite? Give your answer in standard form.
items.markingKey: Correct operation chosen (M1); indices handled correctly (M1); 2.08 × 10³  (A1); sensible rounding/units stated (C1).

items.stem: Lars cycles 197 m, to the nearest metre, in 31 s, to the nearest second. Find the upper and lower bounds of the average speed, and give the speed to a suitable degree of accuracy.
items.markingKey: UB = 197.5/30.5 = 6.4754 (M1 A1); LB = 196.5/31.5 = 6.2381 (M1 A1); both round to 6.0… so a justified accuracy is the value where the bounds agree (R1).
